test_paradigm: Rust, per .claude/rules/testing.md. Every acceptance body is PRE-AUTHORED by DISTILL (feature-delta.md DISTILL sections, distill/test-scenarios.md, distill/red-classification.md); crafters only remove the #[should_panic] marker of the tests the step names, run the body unchanged, confirm the semantic RED before changing production code, implement to the pinned contract (feature-delta.md Interface contracts) and confirm GREEN. Crafters never write, replace, weaken or complete an acceptance body and never invent public API: a missing shape is a blocker surfaced to the orchestrator (CLAUDE.md 'Implement to the design'). The only sanctioned edits to existing (non-pending) tests are the mechanical field renames and literal rewrites the single-cut type change forces, the DD-7 stale goldens listed in DELIVER obligation 2, and the one reversed #348 expectation of DELIVER obligation 3, which is a user-authorized spec change performed by the orchestrator via nw-acceptance-designer. Pure functions get proptest (already authored for both grammars). Every command runs on the metal box (cargo xtask metal run -- ...), never Lima, never --exclusive for tests; this feature has no kvm-tests, guest-placed or native_launcher test. Mutation testing is per-feature (CLAUDE.md: cargo xtask metal run -- cargo xtask mutants --diff origin/main --features integration-tests, kill rate >= 80%): per step scope it with --package and --file over that step's production files, and run the full per-package diff once before the PR. No roadmap step id or issue number in any new identifier, filename or log message (.claude/rules/domain-naming.md). Validator length warnings are cosmetic.

steps.name: ByteSize and CpuQuantity grammars; VolumeSize rebuilt on ByteSize with the whole-GiB refinement
steps.description: Implement the two pure value types exactly as feature-delta.md Interface contracts pins them: ByteSize (u64 bytes; units B, KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB case-insensitive; five typed ParseError variants classified in the pinned order; canonical Display in the largest exactly dividing unit, zero is 0B; serde string) and CpuQuantity (u32 millicores; 500m, decimal cores to three fractional digits, whole cores; four typed variants; canonical Display whole cores when exact else <n>m; serde string). Rebuild VolumeSize::from_str on ByteSize and refuse zero or a non-multiple of 1 GiB; Display delegates to the ByteSize canonical form. Additive: no existing consumer changes, so the workspace stays green. @sizing-review-needed (three types in three files that share one grammar contract and one test binary; kept as one step because the volume refinement is proven by the shared grammar tests).
criteria: byte_size_grammar.rs: all 15 pending tests lose their should_panic and pass unchanged: pinned accept table, canonical display, any count in any unit and case, serde round trip, the five rejection classes and their order, error text, u64 boundary, bare serde number refused naming the expected form, and the_volume_size_is_the_shared_grammar_refined_to_whole_gib (1024MiB accepted as 1GiB; 512MiB, 0GiB, 1.5GiB, 1GB refused)

cpu_quantity_grammar.rs: all 12 pending tests lose their should_panic and pass unchanged: 500m, 0.5 and 0.500 are 500; 2, 2000m and 2.0 are 2000; zero accepted; UnknownSuffix (uppercase M names the lowercase m), TooManyDecimals (0.5000), Overflow at the u32 millicore boundary, Malformed, serde bare number refused, and parse(display(v)) == v

vm_volume_size.rs: the pending test a_whole_gib_written_in_mib_or_bytes_is_the_same_volume_size loses its should_panic marker and passes unchanged (marker removal only, no body edit); text_outside_the_grammar_is_rejected was ALREADY re-drawn (no MiB) by the acceptance designer under the user-authorized spec change R-4, is green today and stays green, and the step does not edit it; every other #348 volume test (round trip in any unit case, TiB/GiB equality, display prefers TiB only when exact, 40MiB refused, overflow, serde rejects invalid) and the volume_value_types.rs bytes and ByteCount tests pass untouched

No public item beyond the pinned ByteSize, ByteSizeParseError, CpuQuantity, CpuQuantityParseError, their constructors and accessors is added; VolumeSize(u64), its derives and bytes() and ByteCount are unchanged; the serde string and archived u64 of every previously admitted volume size are unchanged

steps.implementation_notes: Contract shape pure-function (return-only); no adapter, so no probe. DD-1, DD-2, DD-3 (ADR-0339, ADR-0310 amendment 2026-11-20, ADR-0340); grammar rules live only in feature-delta.md Interface contracts. Start from the DISTILL scaffolds byte_size.rs and cpu_quantity.rs (remove the SCAFFOLD marker and the scaffold-only allow block once real); lib.rs already declares both modules and pins no re-export. Hand-built scanners, no new dependency (bytesize, byte-unit, k8s-openapi, kube_quantity are rejected). Newtype rules: constructors validate and return Result, Display/FromStr/serde agree, no .expect() in library code, thiserror variants each with their own remedy Display. Checked arithmetic for overflow (never wrap). VolumeSize::from_str parses a ByteSize then refuses zero or a non-multiple of 1 GiB, as VolumeSizeParseError (existing shape unchanged). If any #348 test other than the one listed fails after the parser change, surface it to the user; do not edit it. steps.name: Single-cut type change: cpu and memory typed fields from spec to driver, whole-MiB admission, OpenAPI, describe
steps.description: Replace cpu_milli and memory_bytes with CpuQuantity cpu and ByteSize memory in one commit: Resources, both ResourcesInput twins (deny_unknown_fields refuses the removed keys), NodeSpecInput, ResourceEnvelope, ResourcesBody. Admission refuses zero memory and non-whole-MiB memory at Job::from_submit and the service constructor (field memory, DD-8); Node::new keeps only the non-zero check. vcpus_for, cpu_weight_for, the scheduler arithmetic, MemoryPlan callers, the cgroup memory.max write and the Cloud Hypervisor raw byte argument consume .millis()/.bytes(). Regenerate api/openapi.yaml; render::workload_describe prints canonical Memory: and a new CPU: line. Sweep every consumer and fixture: about 242 Rust files, raw TOML/JSON literals, non-.rs goldens and proptest-regression seeds, the four sub-MiB sim fixtures raised to at least 1 MiB, the 35 example TOML specs that tests read, and the stale describe goldens DD-7 makes stale. @sizing-review-needed (cannot be split: Resources, the two input twins and ResourcesBody share fields, so any partial rename leaves the workspace red; the example TOML specs move here because existing tests parse them and the new parser refuses the old keys).
criteria: Through the production parser, submit handler and renderer: cpu = "500m" with memory = "128MiB" is admitted for Job, Service and Schedule shapes and reads back canonically (1024MiB reads back 1GiB with one spec digest); cpu_milli and memory_bytes, a bare number, a missing key and malformed values are refused naming the removed or unknown key and the expected grammar; zero CPU is admitted; zero, 1000B and 1048575B memory refused naming memory; 1048576B admitted

All 27 pending tests of this step lose their should_panic and pass unchanged: workload_resources_spec.rs (10), workload_resources_projections.rs (1), workload_resources_examples.rs (1, now satisfied by the swept example specs), schema_evolution workload_resources_fixtures.rs (2), deploy_workload_resources.rs (5), render_workload_resources.rs (4), workload_resources_wire.rs (3) and workload_resources_submit_refusal.rs (1, a 400 validation naming memory, store unchanged, describe 404); where a body still fails after the marker is removed, confirm the semantic RED first and implement to the contract, never edit the body

Existing golden fixtures decode unchanged: the V1 and V2 hex literals in schema_evolution workload_intent.rs and service_spec.rs and the AllocStatusRow fixtures are byte-identical, only struct-literal field names and types change; a fixture that fails to decode is a blocker to the user, not a re-pin. workload_resources_fixtures.rs proves the archived resources read back as canonical strings

api/openapi.yaml is regenerated (cpu and memory as type string with the pinned examples in ResourcesInput, ResourcesBody and ResourceEnvelope) and the openapi check passes; render::workload_describe prints Memory: 128MiB and CPU: 500m (zero CPU renders 0, no line without a resolved size) and the stale ND295 goldens, guest_stack_mtls_egress and vm_resources_sizing assertions follow the DD-7 canonical forms; the guest still receives raw byte counts (cgroup memory.max, Cloud Hypervisor --memory size=)

Suggested order inside the one commit so each compile error points at the next site: (1) core types (Resources, both ResourcesInput twins, NodeSpecInput, ResourceEnvelope, scheduler, vcpus_for, aggregate admission) then reconcilers, worker, host, sim and control-plane consumers; (2) mechanical rename and literal rewrite across crates/ (about 242 files) plus raw string literals a compile cannot find (node_volume_boundaries.rs, quint_node_volume.rs, tests/conformance/src/gateway.rs, tests/conformance/tests/shared_guest_network_fail_stop_recovery.rs), the non-.rs goldens and proptest-regressions, and the vm_lifecycle.rs generated spec; (3) the 35 example TOML specs under examples/ (33 plus the two under node-local-volume); (4) regenerate OpenAPI: cargo xtask metal run -- cargo run -p overdrive-control-plane --bin openapi -- generate, then -- check; (5) render CPU line and stale goldens. MemoryPlan and reserve_bytes are unchanged; a ByteSize Display is never passed to a foreign protocol (cgroup memory.max and --memory size= stay decimal byte counts from .bytes()). Operator-facing describe change goes through render::workload_describe (the live renderer). Newtype and ordering rules: derive Ord comparisons, saturating arithmetic in the scheduler. The reconcile-trajectory and hydration goldens change only in the field text; any other diff is a defect.
